one_liner: Performs music for a living - on stage, in a studio, at a temple, or at a wedding.
job_roles: Classical Vocalist | Instrumentalist (Classical) | Playback Singer | Session Musician | Band Musician | Orchestra Player | Accompanist | Devotional & Temple Musician | Church Musician | Independent Recording Artist
entrance_exams: Akashvani music audition (grading, not entry) | CUET UG (BA Music)
self_emp_route: Performance fees, session work, private teaching and recording, usually all at once. Practically every Indian musician is self-employed and assembles an income from three or four sources rather than one.
ai_reason: Low exposure and the reason is specific: what is bought here is a live human performing in a room, and generated audio does not substitute for that. Where exposure does bite is recorded and functional music - Session Musician work on advertising beds and library music is the role most at risk, because that market buys a sound rather than a performer. Classical Vocalist, Accompanist and Devotional & Temple Musician are essentially untouched.
role_spread: [Session Musician, Accompanist] higher: conscientiousness, short_term_memory, attention_span / lower: confidence || [Playback Singer, Independent Recording Artist] higher: confidence, extraversion, openness / lower: agreeableness || [Classical Vocalist, Instrumentalist (Classical)] higher: long_term_memory, existential, attention_span / lower: extraversion
path_to_entry: class_11_12: None. Serious training almost always starts in childhood, well before class 11. -> training: Guru-shishya study, a music school, or a BA/MA in music at a university. Years, not months - classical training runs a decade. -> credential: Optional but useful: an Akashvani audition grade, which opens broadcast bookings. It licenses nothing. -> work: Performance, session work, accompaniment, recording and teaching - almost every working musician does several of these.
review_reason: There is no employed version of this profession at any scale in India, so mid_career_lpa - which is EMPLOYED-ONLY by design - describes almost nobody. No sourced figure exists for performance fees, session rates or private tuition income, which is where the entire livelihood sits. This is the sharpest case in the dataset of the schema's salary format failing a profession, and it recurs across most of Sector 10.
nuances: [licensing_body] Null, and the Sangeet Natak Akademi is not one despite being the apex body. It funds, documents and honours; it does not examine or register. The Akashvani grading system is the closest thing to a professional standard and it is voluntary - it opens broadcast bookings and bars nothing. || [years_to_qualify] Six is a conservative reading and applies to the point of earning, not competence. Indian classical training routinely runs ten to fifteen years from a start in childhood, unpaid throughout, which makes it the longest and least-visible runway in this dataset. || [economics] The employed range describes salaried orchestra, ensemble and institutional posts, of which India has very few. It is close to fiction for most of this profession, where income is per performance, per session and per student. That is why the admin_review is required rather than optional.

one_liner: Writes and builds the music itself - for film, advertising, artists and their own releases.
job_roles: Music Producer | Film Music Composer | Songwriter | Lyricist | Arranger | Jingle Composer | Music Programmer | Mixing & Mastering Engineer | Background Score Composer
self_emp_route: Per-project fees, royalties and a home studio. Advertising and corporate work is what pays the bills between the projects people enter this profession for.
ai_reason: The most exposed profession in this sector by a wide margin, and unusually the threat is to the paying middle rather than the entry rung. Generative audio already produces usable library music, advertising beds and background loops, which is exactly what Jingle Composer, Music Programmer and much Arranger work is. Film Music Composer and Background Score Composer are protected by having to serve a director, a scene and a deadline through revisions - and Lyricist by writing in a specific Indian language for a specific voice.
role_spread: [Lyricist, Songwriter] higher: verbal, openness, long_term_memory / lower: logical || [Mixing & Mastering Engineer] higher: logical, attention_span, musical / lower: openness || [Film Music Composer, Background Score Composer] higher: emotional_intelligence, reasoning, conscientiousness / lower: extraversion
path_to_entry: class_11_12: None. -> training: Musical training plus production software. Formal music-production courses exist; most producers are self-taught on the tools. -> portfolio: Released or placed work. In music production credits are the only currency. -> work: Assisting an established composer, advertising and jingle work, or independent releases and artist production.
nuances: [economics] Royalty income is invisible in these figures and can be the larger half of a successful composer's earnings over time. It is also extremely uneven and arrives years late, so it cannot be represented as an annual salary. || [ai_exposure] The band is medium, but the exposure is unusually shaped: it hits FUNCTIONAL music - the anonymous score behind an advertisement or a corporate video - which is precisely the reliable commercial work that funds an Indian composer's career while they build toward film and artist projects.

one_liner: Performs and creates dance - classical, film, contemporary, folk and commercial.
job_roles: Classical Dancer | Contemporary Dancer | Film Choreographer | Assistant Choreographer | Backup Dancer | Commercial & Event Dancer | Folk Dance Performer | Dance Company Member | Movement Director
self_emp_route: Performance fees, film and event bookings, and running a dance school - which in practice is what most classical dancers do, and it is the part that pays reliably.
ai_reason: Among the least exposed professions in the dataset. Dance is a trained body in a physical space, and no part of that is a text or image problem. Synthetic video can depict dancing; it cannot be the dancer a company hires or the choreographer who rehearses forty people. Assistant Choreographer is the only role with any exposure, through pre-visualisation tools.
role_spread: [Film Choreographer, Assistant Choreographer] higher: spatial, extraversion, conscientiousness, emotional_stability / lower: - || [Classical Dancer] higher: long_term_memory, existential, attention_span / lower: extraversion || [Movement Director] higher: reasoning, emotional_intelligence, verbal / lower: bodily
path_to_entry: class_11_12: None. Classical training generally starts in childhood. -> training: Years under a guru, a dance school, or a BA/MA in dance at an institution such as Kalakshetra or Rabindra Bharati. -> performance: Arangetram or equivalent debut for classical forms; auditions and troupe work for commercial dance. -> work: Performance, troupe membership, film and event work, choreography and teaching - nearly always several at once.
review_reason: Performance fees, event rates and dance-school income are the whole livelihood and none is sourced. The record also has nothing on the age profile of performing income, which is the single most important economic fact in a physical performance career and is currently invisible.
nuances: [economics] The employed range describes company and institutional posts, which India has very few of. It also hides a hard fact of this profession: performing income falls with age in a way most careers' do not, and teaching is not a fallback but the intended second half. || [demand_signal] Moderate rather than low because of the volume of commercial work - film, television, weddings and events employ far more dancers than the classical concert circuit does. A student attracted by the classical form should know the paying market is mostly elsewhere.

one_liner: Plays a part in front of an audience or a camera - stage, screen, television or ad film.
job_roles: Stage Actor | Film Actor | Television Actor | Repertory Company Actor | Advertising Film Actor | Improv Performer | Mime Artist | Street Theatre Performer | Background Artist
entrance_exams: National School of Drama entrance | FTII JET
self_emp_route: Almost universal - actors are hired per project with no employment relationship. The exceptions are repertory companies and long-running television serials, both of which offer something closer to a salary.
ai_reason: Low exposure on the composition, and the honest caveat is that synthetic performers are the one place this could change faster than the model suggests. Background Artist and Advertising Film Actor are the exposed roles - crowd replacement and synthetic presenters are already in commercial use. Stage Actor, Repertory Company Actor and Improv Performer are protected by the audience being in the room with a person who might fail.
role_spread: [Repertory Company Actor, Stage Actor] higher: long_term_memory, conscientiousness, bodily, emotional_stability / lower: - || [Background Artist] higher: conscientiousness, attention_span / lower: confidence, openness || [Street Theatre Performer] higher: extraversion, confidence, existential, emotional_stability / lower: -
path_to_entry: class_11_12: None. -> training: Theatre groups and college drama, then optionally NSD, FTII, or a private acting school. NSD requires six prior productions just to apply. -> portfolio: A showreel and a photo portfolio, and registration with casting directors. -> work: Auditions - advertising, television, web series and film. Advertising and television are where steady early income is.
review_reason: Same defect as Digital Content Creator in Sector 9 and Entrepreneur in Sector 5: the income distribution is a power law and a range may be the wrong format entirely. Decide whether to suppress the numbers and state the risk. No sourced figure exists for Indian television, advertising or repertory day rates, which are the realistic income for anyone who does make a living here.
nuances: [entrance_exams] NSD was briefly recorded as this profession's primary_gate and has been removed on review. It takes 26 students a year nationally and almost no working Indian actor went through it, so naming it as THE gate would have told a fifteen-year-old that acting has a door 26 places wide. It does not - it has auditions, which cannot be counted. Recording a famous number because it is the only number available is the opposite of what the gate registry is for. || [economics] A power-law distribution presented as a range, which is close to misleading. A handful earn extraordinarily, a thin layer of television and advertising actors earn a living, and most people who describe themselves as actors earn very little from acting in any given year. || [economics] economics.distribution is 'power_law', which is a statement that the range and the midpoint should not be read as a typical income. A handful earn extraordinarily, a thin layer of television and advertising actors earn a living, and most people who describe themselves as actors earn very little from acting in any given year. The compensation filter does not fire on a power_law record, because deleting a profession on the strength of a number the record itself calls meaningless would be worse than showing it.

one_liner: Reads a room and plays music live to it - clubs, weddings, festivals and events.
job_roles: Club DJ | Wedding & Event DJ | Radio DJ | Turntablist | Electronic Music Producer | Festival Performer | Mobile Disco Operator | Sound & Music Curator (Hospitality)
self_emp_route: This profession is self-employment. Bookings are taken directly or through event agencies, and owning a full sound and lighting rig roughly doubles what a wedding booking pays.
ai_reason: Genuinely two-sided. Electronic Music Producer faces the same generative-audio pressure as the rest of music production, and automated mixing and recommendation already do a creditable job of sequencing tracks. But the paying job is not track selection - it is reading a specific room of drunk, tired or delighted people and changing course, which is why Club DJ, Wedding & Event DJ and Festival Performer are protected. A playlist has never been the competition; a playlist has always existed.
role_spread: [Wedding & Event DJ, Mobile Disco Operator] higher: extraversion, conscientiousness, bodily / lower: openness || [Electronic Music Producer] higher: logical, musical, attention_span / lower: extraversion
path_to_entry: class_11_12: None. -> equipment: Controller, speakers and a laptop. This is the real cost of entry and it is why the figure is not near zero. -> practice: Build sets and a following - mixes online, small venues, and word of mouth in a city. -> work: Residencies, wedding and event bookings, corporate parties and festivals. Wedding season is the income.
nuances: [demand_signal] High, and it rests almost entirely on the Indian wedding market rather than on club culture. That makes the work seasonal and regionally spread rather than concentrated in a few metros, which is unusual for this sector. || [economics] Wedding and event income arrives in a few months of the year and is billed per booking, not per month. Annual figures flatten a shape that a student planning cashflow needs to see.

one_liner: Performs an inherited regional form - wedding bands, temple music, folk theatre, processions.
job_roles: Folk Musician | Wedding Band Musician | Dhol & Percussion Player | Folk Theatre Artist | Temple & Ritual Performer | Puppeteer | Street Performer | Bhajan & Kirtan Singer | Processional Brass Player | Folk Troupe Member
self_emp_route: Performing on own account or as part of a family troupe, taking bookings directly. The step that actually changes income is empanelment with a state culture department or a festival circuit, which converts local rates into touring fees.
ai_reason: The lowest exposure in this sector along with dance, and for the same reason: the work is a human body performing in a physical place, usually as part of a ritual or a celebration whose whole point is that people are present. Recorded music substitutes for a wedding band at the cheap end of the market, but that substitution happened decades ago and is not new.
role_spread: [Puppeteer, Folk Theatre Artist] higher: verbal, long_term_memory, openness / lower: extraversion || [Wedding Band Musician, Processional Brass Player] higher: bodily, conscientiousness / lower: openness
path_to_entry: class_11_12: None. Almost all of these forms are learned within a family or community from childhood. -> training: Apprenticeship within the tradition. Some forms have state academies and guru-shishya schemes funded through the Sangeet Natak Akademi and state culture departments. -> work: Weddings, festivals, temple calendars and processions - work follows the season and the local ritual year. -> recognition: State and national culture-department empanelment, festival circuits and grants, which is what lifts a folk performer above local rates.
review_reason: No sourced income figure exists for any Indian folk performance work - not wedding band rates, not troupe fees, not state empanelment payments. Empanelment is named as the route by which income rises and its value is unknown, which makes the most important advice on this record unquantified.
nuances: [economics] The base layer of Indian performing arts, and the numbers say so. Income is per booking, seasonal, cash and undocumented. This fails the compensation filter, which is correct, and it is listed anyway because it is where a very large number of performing livelihoods actually are. || [demand_signal] Moderate and structurally uneven. Ritual and wedding demand is steady and geographically spread; the audience for long-form folk theatre is shrinking as television and phones absorb the evenings it used to fill. Those two facts point opposite ways and both are true. || [professional_sector] Placed here rather than in Sector 17 with heritage because these are working performers being paid to perform, not custodians interpreting a tradition for study. The intervene-versus-interpret split in DECISIONS.md 2 is what decides it.

one_liner: Makes a live show work - sound, lights, rigging, staging and the running of the event.
job_roles: Live Sound Engineer | Monitor Engineer | Stage Manager | Lighting Operator (Live) | Backline Technician | Stage Rigger | AV Technician | Stage Crew | Event Production Coordinator
self_emp_route: Owning equipment - a PA system, lighting rig or backline - and hiring it out with yourself operating it. Equipment ownership, not seniority, is how income rises in live production.
ai_reason: Low exposure. Mixing a live band in a room with feedback, a bad PA and a singer who moves is a real-time physical problem, and automated mixing tools assume a studio. AV Technician is the most exposed role, since corporate AV is increasingly pre-programmed and automated. Stage Rigger and Backline Technician are untouched - the work is hardware in the air and on the floor.
role_spread: [Stage Manager, Event Production Coordinator] higher: conscientiousness, extraversion, attention_span / lower: bodily || [Stage Rigger] higher: bodily, spatial, conscientiousness / lower: openness
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Any stream, or none. Physics helps with sound and electricity. -> training: A sound or event-technology diploma, or entry as stage crew and learning on the job. Both routes are normal. -> work: Crew for an event production or sound-hire company. Work is per show and heavily seasonal. -> specialisation: Front-of-house sound, monitors, lighting or rigging. Specialising is what separates day-rate crew from booked engineers.
nuances: [demand_signal] High and growing, driven by live events, weddings, corporate conferences and a genuine festival circuit that did not exist fifteen years ago. This is the most reliably employable profession in Sector 10 and the least visible. || [degree_dependency] Certificate, and the honest note is that the diploma matters less than the first crew job. Live production hires people it has seen work, which makes entry easy for anyone near a city with events and nearly impossible remotely.

one_liner: Builds, tunes and repairs instruments - sitars, tablas, harmoniums, guitars, pianos.
job_roles: Instrument Maker (String) | Tabla & Percussion Maker | Harmonium Maker & Repairer | Guitar Luthier | Piano Tuner & Technician | Instrument Repair Technician | Bow Maker | Brass & Wind Instrument Technician
self_emp_route: Own workshop making to order and repairing, selling direct to musicians and shops. A maker with a name among performers charges several times what workshop wages pay.
ai_reason: Essentially unexposed. Instrument making is skilled handwork on natural materials judged by ear, and repair is diagnosis of a physical object in front of you. Nothing in the generative-AI wave touches any part of it. The threats to this trade are real but entirely different: cheap imported factory instruments and a shrinking number of apprentices.
role_spread: [Piano Tuner & Technician] higher: musical, attention_span, logical / lower: openness || [Instrument Maker (String), Guitar Luthier] higher: spatial, bodily, naturalistic / lower: extraversion
path_to_entry: class_11_12: None. The trade is usually inherited or entered as a workshop apprentice. -> training: Apprenticeship in a making workshop - Miraj, Kolkata, Delhi and Chennai are the main Indian centres. -> work: Making or repairing for a workshop, a music shop or a distributor. -> independence: Own workshop, which is where the difference between a wage and a livelihood is in this trade.
review_reason: No sourced income figure for Indian instrument makers or repairers, employed or independent, and the gap between the two is the whole story of this trade. At 4.8 LPA employed with a named independent route and no ceiling, the record currently understates it in exactly the way self_employment.ceiling_lpa was added to prevent.
nuances: [demand_signal] Low, and it is a thin but stable market rather than a collapsing one. The number of makers is falling faster than demand, which is why skilled repairers are genuinely scarce in most Indian cities - a student entering this trade competes with very few people. || [economics] Workshop wages and an independent maker's income are barely the same profession. The employed figure is the floor; the route out of it is a reputation among performers, which takes years and is not purchasable.

one_liner: Makes theatre happen - directing, writing plays, producing and running a company.
job_roles: Theatre Director | Playwright | Dramaturg | Theatre Producer | Drama Facilitator | Applied Theatre Practitioner | Theatre Company Manager | Translation & Adaptation Writer (Theatre)
self_emp_route: Running a company or working project to project on grants, commissions, corporate workshops and applied theatre contracts. Workshop and facilitation work is what most Indian theatre-makers actually live on.
ai_reason: The lowest digital exposure in the dataset alongside the trades, and the highest clarity in this sector. The job is deciding what a play should mean now, to this audience, in this city - then getting thirty people to agree and rehearse it. Playwright is the only role with real exposure, and even there the constraint is that a play must survive being spoken aloud by actors for two hours.
role_spread: [Playwright, Translation & Adaptation Writer (Theatre)] higher: verbal, openness, long_term_memory / lower: extraversion || [Drama Facilitator, Applied Theatre Practitioner] higher: emotional_intelligence, agreeableness, conscientiousness / lower: confidence || [Theatre Producer, Theatre Company Manager] higher: conscientiousness, logical, extraversion / lower: openness
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Any stream. -> degree: Any bachelor's degree - NSD requires one in any discipline to apply, plus six prior productions. -> training: NSD, a university drama department, or years inside a working theatre group. The group route is the commonest. -> work: Directing for a company, applied theatre and workshop facilitation, and grant-funded productions. Very few make a living from productions alone.
review_reason: No sourced figure for Indian theatre grant, commission or facilitation rates, which are the actual income here. The record also cannot show what proportion of practitioners hold a second job, which for this profession is the most decision-relevant fact there is.
nuances: [demand_signal] Low, and honestly so. India has few funded theatre companies, almost no commercial theatre outside a handful of cities, and shrinking state culture budgets. The work exists and is done; it is rarely a whole income, and applied theatre and corporate workshops are what make it viable. || [economics] Understated even by this sector's standards, because grant-funded and commission income is lumpy and most practitioners hold a second job. The figures assume a practice subsidised by facilitation and workshop work, which is the normal case.

one_liner: The person in the photograph or on the ramp - the presence is the product.
job_roles: Fashion Model | Ramp & Runway Model | Print & Commercial Model | Advertising Model | Fit Model | Promotional Model | Catalogue Model | Parts Model
self_emp_route: Almost every model is independent - paid per shoot or per show, through an agency that takes a commission, with no employment relationship. There is no salaried version of this work.
ai_reason: The exposure model here measures retrievable knowledge and digital skill, and by that measure modelling scores low because the work is physical presence. That understates a real and already-arrived threat: generative image models are replacing catalogue and e-commerce modelling, where the client needs a body wearing a garment and does not need it to be a particular person. Ramp, campaign and celebrity-adjacent work is far less substitutable.
path_to_entry: entry: A portfolio, a comp card and physical criteria set by the client. There is no course and no qualification -> work: Registration with a modelling agency, or direct casting calls -> work: Portfolio built through test shoots, then paid catalogue and commercial work -> work: Ramp, campaign and brand work for the small number who reach it
review_reason: economics.distribution is power_law and the bands are a per-shoot rate multiplied by an assumed booking frequency that is not sourced. A handful of models earn very large sums, a thin layer earn a living from catalogue and commercial work, and most people who describe themselves as models earn very little from modelling in any given year. Decide how the application presents this - and note the second risk on the record: generative image models are already displacing the catalogue segment that most working models depend on.
nuances: [professional_sector] Performing Arts & Music, beside Actor & Performer, because in both the person IS the instrument and the work is presence in front of an audience or a camera. Two alternatives were considered: Sector 8 beside Fashion Designer, rejected because a model designs nothing; and Sector 9 beside Voice Artist & Broadcast Presenter, which is defensible and was not chosen because ramp work is not media production. || [economics] There is no annual salary for this work and quoting one would be false. What is sourced is PER-ENGAGEMENT: roughly 2,000 to 30,000 rupees per shoot for most commercial work in India, with international brand campaigns reaching a lakh and above, from an Indian modelling platform's published rate guide. The annual bands here are that per-shoot rate multiplied by an assumed and unsourced number of bookings, which is why distribution is power_law and an admin_review is open. || [ai_exposure] The low band is correct by this repo's model and misleading on its own. Generative image tools are already substituting for catalogue and e-commerce modelling - the segment where most working models actually earn - because the client needs a garment shown on a body, not a specific person. The composition model cannot express substitution of a physical presence by a generated image, and the application should carry that warning from this nuance rather than from the band. || [self_employment] Booking-to-booking independent work with an agency commission is the normal arrangement, not the exception. There is no employed version of this profession to compare against, which is part of why the earnings bands describe nobody in particular.
